description: We are team Alstronauts 🚀. We're a fully formed, multidisciplinary team of AI enthusiasts, developers, & Earth lovers ready to tackle the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge at NASA Space Apps. Our goal is to leverage advanced AI & ML to analyze complex Earth observation datasets and uncover vital environmental trends. With our blend of ML engineering, software dev, & data analysis, we're ready to decode our home planet! 🌍 (Note: Our team is fully complete).
summary: EARTHSCOPE turns a simple question — "Is precipitation decreasing in Jordan?" — into a statistically tested answer built from real NASA data. Users pick one of 19 Earth-science variables, each explained in plain language, and any country, region or drawn area. EARTHSCOPE fetches 45 years of monthly NASA POWER data (MERRA-2 / CERES) for every grid cell inside the region, builds an area-weighted time series and tests it with the Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope with 95% confidence intervals, autocorrelation-corrected regression and the Seasonal Kendall test. Every result comes with one plain sentence, the rate of change per decade and whether it is statistically significant; non-significant trends are shown too, with the number of years of data needed to detect them. Users can compare regions (opposite trends are only claimed when both are significant), explore a 3D globe of 640 trend tests per variable, relate variables with lagged correlations, ask a rule-based AI Scientist that only uses computed numbers, and export a scientific report. It covers all four challenge steps and helps students tell real environmental change from noise.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

EARTHSCOPE is a web app that lets students act as Earth-system trend detectives. You ask a question about a place and a variable (for example "Is precipitation decreasing in Jordan?") and EARTHSCOPE answers with real NASA data: what changed, by how much, and whether the change is statistically real or could be natural year-to-year variation.

HOW IT WORKS (the four challenge steps)

1. Identify variables: 19 Earth-science variables (air and land temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, water vapor, aerosols, ozone, snow, sea surface temperature, sea ice, NDVI and more), each with a plain-language definition and the NASA mission or model behind it.

2. Acquire data for a region: choose a country, region, drawn box or coordinates. EARTHSCOPE samples every NASA POWER grid cell inside the real country border, weights cells by area and builds a monthly regional series for 1981–2025.

3. Time series: annual values with the trend line and 95% confidence band, the monthly record, deseasonalised anomalies and a seasonal-cycle comparison.

4. Rate of change and significance: Mann-Kendall test with Sen's slope (95% CI), checked against autocorrelation-corrected regression (AR1), the Hamed–Rao test and the Seasonal Kendall test, plus how many years of data are needed to detect the trend.

FEATURES

- One plain sentence for every result, built only from computed numbers (e.g. "Cameroon is warming by about 0.36 °C every decade — a statistically significant trend").

- Regional comparison with a forest plot; "opposite trends" are only claimed when both regions are significant.

- 3D Earth that unfolds into a map, with 640 trend tests per variable (Benjamini–Hochberg FDR q = 0.05) and NASA GIBS imagery.

- Relationship Lab: lagged correlations with a "correlation is not causation" warning.

- AI Scientist: a rule-based assistant that answers only from computed results and labels every explanation as an untested hypothesis.

- Scientific report export (PDF, CSV, JSON) and CSV import from Giovanni, AppEEARS, NOAA CDO and KNMI.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

EARTHSCOPE teaches how scientists decide whether a change is real. It never hides a non-significant result: for example, Jordan's yearly rainfall fell by about 1.90 mm/yr per decade (1981–2025), but p = 0.63, so the data are consistent with no trend, and about 94 years of data would be needed to detect a trend that small.

TOOLS

React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, three.js (custom globe-to-map shader), d3, zustand, Vitest (697 automated tests; statistics cross-checked against SciPy and pymannkendall). Hosted on Netlify; NASA POWER and GIBS are called directly from the browser.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Only real data (every series shows its source and retrieval date; no fabricated numbers), one significance rule everywhere (p < 0.05 for one series, FDR q < 0.05 for maps), significance never shown by colour alone, accessibility and mobile layouts. Limitations: regional means are grid-cell samples of the MERRA-2 reanalysis, trends are linear, and Earthdata-login products are analysed through CSV import.

AI USE

AI coding assistants (Claude) helped write the code, documentation and demo slides. The in-app AI Scientist is rule-based, not a language model. Demo screenshots are real captures of the app.

Live app: https://earthscope-space-apps.netlify.app

Source code: https://github.com/basharmukbel1/earthscope
